_schema.notation: dataset -> scene name -> camera dir name (e.g. 'cam01') -> {op_type: [entries]}. Each entry is applied in list order, matching the functions in utilities/within_reid_operations.py. Empty list = nothing to do for that op type.

remove._meaning: delete a track. Whole track if no frames given; a frame window [start_frame,end_frame] inclusive if given (excise a spurious stretch, keep the rest).

merge._meaning: fuse id_a+id_b into one id (output_id, default id_a). split_frame: if given, frames < split_frame come from id_a and frames >= split_frame from id_b (required if the two tracks frame ranges overlap); if null, the two tracks must be non-overlapping and their union is taken.

split._meaning: cut one id into two: frames >= split_frame move to new_id (inverse of merge, use when one id silently swapped identity mid-track)

swap._meaning: exchange id_a and id_b over a frame window [start_frame,end_frame] inclusive (id-steal at a crossing; non-destructive, both ids survive)

rename._meaning: relabel one id, no other track touched

_schema.execution_order: Within a camera, ops apply in this fixed order regardless of listing: split -> remove -> merge -> swap -> rename. Use temp ids (e.g. 20,21) in split.new_id to stage tracks, then merge them into the final id. All ops act on body_data/person_<id>.npz only (mask_data.npz/json_data are legacy and left untouched).
